staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against this staged vulnerable checkout.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502932 (freeradius-server): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer_dns [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502932
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 22-byte DNS packet `44 81 9a 97 00 00 00 00 60 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 2d 00 00 dc dc 23`. `fr_dns_decode_proto()` forwards that raw buffer into `fr_dns_decode()`. The header stores `qdcount = 0`, `ancount = 0`, `nscount = 0x6000`, and `arcount = 0`, so the earlier question and answer `decode_record()` calls consume nothing after the 12-byte DNS header. `fr_dns_decode()` then makes the NS-section call `decode_record(..., packet = full_packet + 12, packet_len = 10, ..., counter = full_packet + 8)`. That 10-byte section slice is the first NS RR: root label `00`, `type = 0x0001`, `class = 0x002d`, `ttl = 0x0000dcdc`, and a final trailing byte `0x23`. The outer `fr_struct_from_network()` call decodes those fixed RR fields, uses the key field `type = 1` to select dictionary `STRUCT a`, and recurses into that substruct with only the last one-byte slice left. Vulnerable `fr_struct_from_network()` treats `STRUCT a` as length-prefixed (`length=uint16`) and immediately executes `struct_len = (p[0] << 8) | p[1];` without first checking that at least two bytes remain. Because the recursive call's `data_len` is 1, `p[1]` is one byte past the 22-byte packet buffer and AddressSanitizer reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 at `src/lib/util/struct.c:110`. The staged patch fixes the exact obligation by adding `if ((end - p) < 2) { ... goto unknown; }` before the 16-bit length read.

source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path that turns attacker-controlled DNS header bytes into a loop bound for record decoding.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 22-byte packet `44 81 9a 97 00 00 00 00 60 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 2d 00 00 dc dc 23`. In `fr_dns_decode()`, the exact witness gives `qdcount = 0` and `ancount = 0`, so the NS-section call is `decode_record(..., packet = full_packet + 12, packet_len = 10, ..., counter = full_packet + 8)`. `counter` therefore reads header bytes `60 00` while `packet` names the 10-byte post-header slice to be parsed as NS records.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The nested length-prefixed substruct decoder reads a 16-bit length header without first checking that at least two bytes remain in the current slice.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `if ((end - p) < 2) { FR_PROTO_TRACE("Insufficient room for length header"); goto unknown; }` immediately before this line.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. In the nested `STRUCT a` decode, this statement reads the second byte of a 16-bit length header even though the recursive slice contains only one remaining byte.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `src/lib/util/struct.c:110:30` on address `0x603000000236`, which is 0 bytes to the right of the 22-byte packet buffer `[0x603000000220, 0x603000000236)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first concrete attacker-derived control value on the crashing path: the NSCOUNT bytes `60 00` become `count = 24576`, which is why the decoder enters the NS-record loop at all.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact witness stores `60 00` at DNS header offsets 8-9, and in the NS-section call `fr_dns_decode()` passes `counter = full_packet + 8` while `packet = full_packet + 12` and `packet_len = 10`.

parser_admitted.description: The 22-byte witness has already been admitted to the DNS decoder here. `fr_dns_decode_proto()` initializes `packet_ctx` and forwards the raw packet directly into `fr_dns_decode()`; the optional `fr_dns_packet_ok` prefilter above is disabled under `#if 0`, so malformed section counts are not rejected before record parsing begins.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is closed from the staged source, DNS dictionary, exact `poc` bytes, saved ASan traces, and `reproduction_report.json` only.

The saved ASan allocation context belongs to libFuzzer's input-buffer allocation (`malloc` / `operator new` / `RunOneTest`), not project code, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.allocation_context` is `null` even though the overread extent itself is fully grounded by the saved 22-byte region bounds.

The saved runtime artifacts do not dump intermediate locals like `key_vp` or `labels_len`; those values are deterministically reconstructed from the exact witness bytes and the staged vulnerable DNS dictionary (`type = 1` selects `STRUCT a`, whose payload is `length=uint16`).

coarse_trace.summary: `fr_dns_decode_proto()` installs packet context for the attacker-controlled 22-byte buffer and forwards it into `fr_dns_decode()` without an active `fr_dns_packet_ok()` prefilter.

The header gives `qdcount = 0` and `ancount = 0`, so `fr_dns_decode()` reaches the NS-section call with `packet = full_packet + 12`, `packet_len = 10`, and `counter = full_packet + 8`; `decode_record()` materializes `nscount = 0x6000` from those header bytes and starts parsing the first 10-byte NS RR slice.
The outer RR parser consumes the fixed fields `name`, `type = 1`, `class = 0x002d`, and `ttl = 0x0000dcdc`, leaving only one payload byte and recording the key field needed for substruct dispatch.
The key field `type = 1` resolves to dictionary `STRUCT a`, so `fr_struct_from_network()` recurses into a length-prefixed child substruct with `data_len = 1`.
The nested `length=uint16` decoder reads `p[1]` while forming `struct_len`, overrunning the 22-byte packet buffer and producing the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the exact witness, `fr_dns_decode()` first sees `qdcount = 0` and `ancount = 0`, so the earlier question and answer calls consume nothing and the NS-section call is `decode_record(..., packet = full_packet + 12, packet_len = 10, ..., counter = full_packet + 8)`. This step reads that attacker-controlled header field through `counter`, and bytes `60 00` materialize `count = 0x6000`.

Inside this `decode_record()` frame, the locals are `p = packet` and `end = packet + packet_len`. For the NS-section call above, that means `packet = full_packet + 12` and `packet_len = 10`, so at the first loop iteration (`i = 0`) the only pre-call guard `p >= end` is false and `fr_struct_from_network()` receives exactly the 10-byte slice `00 00 01 00 2d 00 00 dc dc 23`.

For the RR `name` field, the first byte is `0x00`, so `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` sets `next = data + 1` and `labels_len = 1`. The outer RR parser therefore consumes a one-byte root label and leaves 9 bytes for the remaining fixed fields and payload.

On the second RR child, `child` is the key field `type`. `decode_value()` reads bytes `00 01` as `type = 1`, and because this child is the RR key field the caller stores that decoded value in `key_vp` for later substruct selection.

fine_trace.code: p += slen;    /* not always the same as child->flags.length */
fine_trace.note: The next fixed RR fields consume `class = 0x002d` (2 bytes) and `ttl = 0x0000dcdc` (4 bytes). After those advances, the original 10-byte RR slice has only the last byte `0x23` left, so `end - p == 1` before substruct dispatch.

Because `key_vp->data == 1`, the dictionary resolves the RR payload to `STRUCT a`, and `STRUCT a` is declared with `length=uint16`. The outer parser recurses into that child with `p` at the lone trailing byte and `end - p == 1`.

Root cause and sink. In the nested call, `parent` is `STRUCT a`, so `da_is_length_field(parent)` is true and the decoder immediately treats the current bytes as a 16-bit length header. Here `data_len == 1`, so there is no second header byte, but this line reads `p[1]` before any two-byte availability check. AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 1` here at the first byte past the 22-byte packet buffer. The staged patch adds the exact `(end - p) < 2` guard immediately before this read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes at the source level. The staged patch inserts `if ((end - p) < 2) { ... goto unknown; }` immediately before `struct_len = (p[0] << 8) | p[1];`, which is the exact missing obligation on the witnessed path. Stage 02 did not perform fixed-version dynamic validation.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan crash location is `fr_struct_from_network /src/freeradius-server/src/lib/util/struct.c:110:30`, which is the exact project-side sink recorded here.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved project stack is `fr_struct_from_network (nested) -> fr_struct_from_network (outer RR parser) -> decode_record -> fr_dns_decode -> fr_dns_decode_proto`, and the fine trace fills in the source-visible RR-field parsing and dictionary-driven `type = 1` substruct selection between those frames.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Header bytes `60 00` drive the NS-section loop, RR bytes `00 01` select `STRUCT a`, and the resulting one-byte remainder reaches the nested `fr_struct_from_network()` call as `p`, where the missing two-byte guard causes the crashing `p[1]` read.

format.name: 22-byte DNS packet
format.contract: Use the exact 22-byte witness `44 81 9a 97 00 00 00 00 60 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 2d 00 00 dc dc 23`. This GT is grounded only for that singular packet: bytes 8-9 must remain `60 00` so `decode_record()` materializes `count = 0x6000` for the NS section, bytes 12-20 must remain `00 00 01 00 2d 00 00 dc dc` so outer RR parsing consumes exactly 9 bytes (`name`, `type = 1`, `class`, `ttl`), and final byte `23` must remain the lone byte passed to the nested `length=uint16` substruct decoder. That exact one-byte remainder is what makes `struct_len = (p[0] << 8) | p[1]` read past the 22-byte packet buffer.
